chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Concerning two men who intentionally killed a man, and he had two heirs, then one of the two heirs pardoned,

So he said: “If some of the heirs pardon them, killing is averted from them, and from the blood-money there is deducted according to the share of the one who pardoned, and the two of them shall pay the remainder from their own wealth to the one who did not pardon.”
And he said: “The pardon of every share-holder is valid.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood-money owed in place of retaliation
key_terms.الْأَوْلِيَاءِ: the heirs or legal guardians entitled to claim retribution or pardon
key_terms.حِصَّةِ: the apportioned share due to a particular heir
key_terms.دُرِئَ: was averted or removed; here, the death penalty is lifted
key_terms.ذِي سَهْمٍ: one who possesses a legal share in the claim
key_terms.عَفْوُ: pardon or remission of one’s legal claim
key_terms.وَلِيَّانِ: two heirs or legal claimants of the slain person

ai.seo_question: If one heir forgives in a murder case, does qisas still apply and how is the diyah calculated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding intentional killing when the slain person has multiple heirs. If one heir pardons, the death penalty is removed, and only the remaining portion of the diyah corresponding to the non-pardoning heir’s share is to be paid. It also establishes that each heir possessing a legal share has the authority to grant pardon regarding his portion.
